datasets.title: Chicago census tracts: median household income
datasets.description: 856 census tracts that intersect the City of Chicago boundary, with median household income (US dollars), as polygons. The tracts are whole tracts, so some extend beyond the city limits and over Lake Michigan.
datasets.source: US Census Bureau: American Community Survey 2018-2022 5-year estimates (table B19013) with 2022 TIGER/Line census tract boundaries, selected where they intersect the City of Chicago boundary (the tracts are not cut at the boundary). Retrieved with the tidycensus and tigris R packages.
datasets.licence: Public domain (work of the US federal government)
datasets.attribution: Source: US Census Bureau, 2018-2022 American Community Survey 5-year estimates (median household income, table B19013) and 2022 TIGER/Line census tract boundaries.
datasets.notice: This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau.

variables.name: GEOID
variables.description: The tract's unique 11-digit census code: 2 digits for the state (17 = Illinois), 3 for the county (031 = Cook County) and 6 for the tract. Use it to join other US Census data to these tracts. It is text, not a number, so keep any leading zeros.

variables.name: NAME
variables.description: The tract's name, for example 'Census Tract 7401; Cook County; Illinois'. Tract numbers are only unique within a county.

variables.name: median_income
variables.description: Median household income of the tract, in US dollars: the income that splits the tract's households into a richer half and a poorer half. It is an estimate from the American Community Survey 2018-2022 five-year data (table B19013), adjusted to 2022 dollars. Because it comes from a sample survey, each figure carries a margin of error that is not included here. The Census Bureau reports incomes of $250,000 or more as 250,001, so that value means 'at least $250,000' (one tract here).

variables.name: geometry
variables.description: The outline of the tract (a polygon), in NAD83 longitude and latitude, for mapping. Tracts here are selected where they touch the City of Chicago boundary and are not cut to it, so they can include suburban land and part of Lake Michigan beyond the city limits.

datasets.title: City of Chicago boundary
datasets.description: The City of Chicago boundary as a single polygon.
datasets.source: US Census Bureau: 2022 TIGER/Line cartographic boundary file for places (Illinois), Chicago. Retrieved with the tigris R package.
datasets.licence: Public domain (work of the US federal government)
datasets.attribution: Source: US Census Bureau, 2022 TIGER/Line cartographic boundary file (places).

variables.name: NAME
variables.description: The name of the place: Chicago.

variables.name: geometry
variables.description: The City of Chicago boundary as a single polygon, in NAD83 longitude and latitude. It is the Census Bureau's cartographic boundary (a simplified outline that excludes the part of Lake Michigan inside the legal city limits), so it is useful for drawing the city but is not exactly the legal boundary.

datasets.title: The Childhood Lottery: England upper-tier local authorities
datasets.description: 153 upper-tier local authorities in England (polygons) with the Children's Commissioner's Childhood Lottery measures: 128 metrics (values and 0-10 scores) across six pillars plus an overall score, one row per authority. See childhood_lottery_metrics for what each column means.
datasets.source: Children's Commissioner for England, The Childhood Lottery (published 19 October 2026), full dataset workbook (https://www.childrenscommissioner.gov.uk/the-childhood-lottery/), reshaped from long to wide (one row per local authority; _value and _score columns per metric; Yes/No answers coded 1/0). Boundaries: ONS Counties and Unitary Authorities (December 2025) Boundaries UK BGC, England only, British National Grid, simplified to 100 m for teaching.
datasets.licence: Free to download from the Children's Commissioner (no formal licence stated); ONS boundaries under the Open Government Licence v3.0
datasets.attribution: Source: Children's Commissioner for England, The Childhood Lottery (2026). Boundaries: Office for National Statistics licensed under the Open Government Licence v.3.0. Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right 2025.
datasets.notice: The Children's Commissioner publishes this dataset for free download but states no formal licence ("All rights reserved"). Klausmate redistributes it, unaltered in content, for teaching with the source credited. Boundaries contain OS data © Crown copyright and database right 2025.

datasets.source: Children's Commissioner for England, The Childhood Lottery (published 19 October 2026), full dataset workbook (https://www.childrenscommissioner.gov.uk/the-childhood-lottery/), reshaped from long to wide (one row per local authority; _value and _score columns per metric; Yes/No answers coded 1/0).

variables.name: pillar
variables.description: The theme the metric belongs to: Better world, Family, Health, Education jobs and skills, Care, Community, or Overall total score.

variables.name: metric
variables.description: The name of the metric as the Children's Commissioner gives it.

variables.name: value_col
variables.description: The name of the column in the childhood_lottery data that holds this metric's value (the raw measure).

variables.name: score_col
variables.description: The name of the column that holds the metric's 0 to 10 score. It is blank when the metric is not scored.

variables.name: description
variables.description: What the metric measures, the year, and which direction is better, in the Commissioner's words.

variables.name: value_type
variables.description: The unit of the value, for example a percentage, a rate per 10,000 children, or a yes/no response.

variables.name: scored
variables.description: Yes if the metric is turned into a score and counts towards the overall score; No if it is shown for information only.

variables.name: source
variables.description: The organisation that produced the underlying data, for example DfE, ONS or Defra.

variables.name: england_average
variables.description: The average for England, in the metric's own units, where the Commissioner gives one.

variables.name: notes
variables.description: Extra notes from the Commissioner, such as the share of authorities that said yes to a yes/no question.

datasets.title: Birmingham LSOAs: change in the share of the Black African population 2001-2011, for multilevel modelling
datasets.description: 659 Lower layer Super Output Areas (2021 geography) in Birmingham (polygons), the modelling rows for a multilevel model: the outcome y_change (the change from 2001 to 2011 in the percentage of Birmingham's Black African population living in the LSOA, in percentage points) and a normalised version (asinh(y_change / 0.05), the same in both periods), the 2001 Black African percentage, the IMD 2010 score (also as twentieths of Birmingham's LSOAs, imd_q20_2010) and the 2025 score, rank, decile and twentieths (imd_q20_2025), plus the MSOA ethnic diversity, ward tenure and constituency 2019 (notional) and 2024 vote variables copied down, with MSOA, ward and constituency codes. Both datasets use the same 2021 LSOAs, 2021 MSOAs, 2022 wards and 2024 constituencies, so the variance at each level can be compared between the two periods. Counts are whole numbers and other numbers are rounded to three decimal places.
datasets.source: Office for National Statistics (via Nomis): Census 2001 tables KS006 (ethnic group) and KS018 (tenure, output areas), Census 2011 tables KS201EW (ethnic group) and KS402EW (tenure, output areas) and Census 2021 tables TS021 (ethnic group) and TS054 (tenure) for the fixed geography for Birmingham; ONS lookups between 2001, 2011 and 2021 output areas, and from output areas to LSOAs, MSOAs, wards and 2024 constituencies; MHCLG English Indices of Deprivation 2010 (all domains file, 2001 LSOAs); MHCLG English Indices of Deprivation 2025 (File 7); ONS December 2021 LSOA boundaries (BGC, generalised and clipped), British National Grid. House of Commons Library, Election Results (general elections 12 December 2019, notional result on the 2024 boundaries, and 4 July 2024, https://electionresults.parliament.uk), under the Open Parliament Licence v3.0. variables.name: lsoa21cd
variables.description: Code of the LSOA (Lower layer Super Output Area, 2021 boundaries): a small area, typically with 1,000 to 3,000 residents. Each row of the data is one LSOA. Use the code to join other data to these rows.

variables.name: lsoa21nm
variables.description: Name of the LSOA, for example 'Birmingham 050F'.

variables.name: msoa21cd
variables.description: Code of the MSOA (Middle layer Super Output Area, 2021) that contains the LSOA. An MSOA is made up of several LSOAs (usually five) and typically has 5,000 to 15,000 residents. Useful as a grouping level in a multilevel model.

variables.name: msoa21nm
variables.description: Name of the MSOA, for example 'Birmingham 050'.

variables.name: ward22cd
variables.description: Code of the electoral ward (2022 boundaries) where most of the LSOA's residents live. Wards and LSOAs do not always fit exactly (about a quarter of these LSOAs have residents in more than one ward), so each LSOA is given its main ward. MSOAs and wards also overlap, so they are crossed rather than nested.

variables.name: ward22nm
variables.description: Name of that ward.

variables.name: pcon_cd
variables.description: Code of the parliamentary constituency (2024 boundaries) where most of the LSOA's residents live. There are 10 in the data. Hodge Hill and Solihull North also covers part of Solihull, outside Birmingham.

variables.name: pcon_nm
variables.description: Name of that constituency.

variables.name: geometry
variables.description: The outline of the LSOA, held in British National Grid coordinates (EPSG:27700), for mapping.

variables.name: pop_2001
variables.description: Number of usual residents of the LSOA at the 2001 census. The 2001 census counted people in older output areas, so the counts have been re-allocated to the 2021 LSOAs in proportion to population and rounded to whole numbers; they can differ slightly from published figures where area boundaries changed.

variables.name: pop_2011
variables.description: Number of usual residents of the LSOA at the 2011 census. The 2011 census counted people in older output areas, so the counts have been re-allocated to the 2021 LSOAs in proportion to population and rounded to whole numbers; they can differ slightly from published figures where area boundaries changed.

variables.name: ba_2001
variables.description: Number of residents of the LSOA who gave their ethnic group as Black African at the 2001 census. The 2001 census counted people in older output areas, so the counts have been re-allocated to the 2021 LSOAs in proportion to population and rounded to whole numbers; they can differ slightly from published figures where area boundaries changed.

variables.name: ba_2011
variables.description: Number of residents of the LSOA who gave their ethnic group as Black African at the 2011 census. The 2011 census counted people in older output areas, so the counts have been re-allocated to the 2021 LSOAs in proportion to population and rounded to whole numbers; they can differ slightly from published figures where area boundaries changed.

variables.name: pop_2022
variables.description: Estimated number of residents in mid-2022, taken from the Index of Multiple Deprivation 2025 data.

variables.name: pct_ba_2001
variables.group: The outcome: change in the Black African population
variables.description: Black African residents as a percentage of all residents of the LSOA in 2001: 100 × ba_2001 / pop_2001. This describes the make-up of the area. It is not the same as the LSOA's share of the city's group (ba_share).

variables.name: pct_ba_2011
variables.group: The outcome: change in the Black African population
variables.description: Black African residents as a percentage of all residents of the LSOA in 2011: 100 × ba_2011 / pop_2011.

variables.name: ba_share_2001
variables.group: The outcome: change in the Black African population
variables.description: The LSOA's share of Birmingham's whole Black African population in 2001: 100 × ba_2001 divided by the city total. The shares add up to 100 across the LSOAs.

variables.name: ba_share_2011
variables.group: The outcome: change in the Black African population
variables.description: The LSOA's share of Birmingham's whole Black African population in 2011.

variables.name: y_change
variables.group: The outcome: change in the Black African population
variables.description: The outcome. ba_share_2011 minus ba_share_2001, in percentage points. A positive value means the LSOA now holds a larger share of the city's Black African population than before; a negative value, a smaller share. This is a change in share, so an LSOA can gain residents and still have a negative value if the city's group grew faster. It adds up to zero across Birmingham.

variables.name: y_change_asinh
variables.group: The outcome: change in the Black African population
variables.description: y_change on a transformed scale: asinh(y_change / 0.05), the same in both Birmingham files. Most changes are small and a few are large; the transformation pulls in the extremes so that the outcome behaves better in a linear model. Zero still means no change and the sign is kept, but the units are no longer percentage points.

variables.name: imd_score_2010
variables.description: Index of Multiple Deprivation score from the 2010 release: the higher the score, the more deprived the area. It was published for older LSOAs, and has been carried to the 2021 LSOAs through output areas as a population-weighted average where LSOAs changed. Scores from different releases are on different scales, so compare ranks or groups rather than raw values across releases.

variables.name: imd_q20_2010
variables.description: The 2010 score as twentieths of Birmingham's own LSOAs: 1 is the most deprived twentieth and 20 the least deprived, with about 33 LSOAs in each. It is relative to Birmingham, not England, and is intended as a grouping variable.

variables.name: imd_score_2025
variables.description: Index of Multiple Deprivation 2025 score, published for the 2021 LSOAs: the higher, the more deprived.

variables.name: imd_rank_2025
variables.description: IMD 2025 rank among all 33,755 LSOAs in England. 1 is the most deprived.

variables.name: imd_decile_2025
variables.description: IMD 2025 decile for England: 1 is the most deprived 10% of LSOAs in England, 10 the least deprived. Most Birmingham LSOAs fall in the lower deciles.

variables.name: imd_q20_2025
variables.description: The IMD 2025 score as twentieths of Birmingham's own LSOAs: 1 is the most deprived twentieth and 20 the least deprived, about 33 LSOAs each. Relative to Birmingham, not England.

variables.name: msoa_div_2001
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: Ethnic diversity of the MSOA in 2001, measured by the Simpson index: 1 minus the sum of the squared shares of 13 ethnic groups that can be compared across the censuses. It is the chance that two randomly chosen residents belong to different groups: 0 means everyone is in one group and values near 1 mean many groups of similar size. It includes the Black African group, so it is partly related to the outcome.

variables.name: msoa_div_2011
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: The same diversity measure for the MSOA in 2011.

variables.name: msoa_div_chg
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: msoa_div_2011 minus msoa_div_2001: the change in diversity.

variables.description: Percentage of households in the ward in 2001 that rent from a council or housing association (social renting). The 2001 figure has been rebuilt for the 2022 wards from small areas. All LSOAs in a ward share one value.

variables.name: ward_social_2011
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: Percentage of households in the ward in 2011 that were social renters.

variables.name: ward_social_chg
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: ward_social_2011 minus ward_social_2001, in percentage points.

variables.name: ward_private_2001
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: Percentage of households in the ward in 2001 that rent from a private landlord or letting agency. (Other private renting and living rent-free are not included, so that the measure matches across censuses.)

variables.name: ward_private_2011
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: Percentage of households in the ward in 2011 that rented from a private landlord or letting agency.

variables.name: ward_private_chg
variables.group: Higher-level variables (the same value for every LSOA in the area)
variables.description: ward_private_2011 minus ward_private_2001, in percentage points.

datasets.title: Birmingham LSOAs: change in the share of the Black African population 2011-2021, for multilevel modelling
datasets.description: 659 Lower layer Super Output Areas (2021 geography) in Birmingham (polygons), the modelling rows for a multilevel model: the outcome y_change (the change from 2011 to 2021 in the percentage of Birmingham's Black African population living in the LSOA, in percentage points) and a normalised version (asinh(y_change / 0.05), the same in both periods), the 2011 Black African percentage, the IMD 2019 score (also as twentieths of Birmingham's LSOAs, imd_q20_2019) and the 2025 score, rank, decile and twentieths (imd_q20_2025), plus the MSOA ethnic diversity, ward tenure and constituency 2019 (notional) and 2024 vote variables copied down, with MSOA, ward and constituency codes. Both datasets use the same 2021 LSOAs, 2021 MSOAs, 2022 wards and 2024 constituencies, so the variance at each level can be compared between the two periods. Counts are whole numbers and other numbers are rounded to three decimal places.
datasets.source: Office for National Statistics (via Nomis): Census 2011 tables KS201EW (ethnic group) and KS402EW (tenure, output areas) and Census 2021 tables TS021 (ethnic group) and TS054 (tenure) for Birmingham; ONS lookups between 2001, 2011 and 2021 output areas, and from output areas to LSOAs, MSOAs, wards and 2024 constituencies; MHCLG English Indices of Deprivation 2019 (File 7, 2011 LSOAs); MHCLG English Indices of Deprivation 2025 (File 7); ONS December 2021 LSOA boundaries (BGC, generalised and clipped), British National Grid. House of Commons Library, Election Results (general elections 12 December 2019, notional result on the 2024 boundaries, and 4 July 2024, https://electionresults.parliament.uk), under the Open Parliament Licence v3.0.
